newsitem.title: USA: Texas April sales tax payments down vs April '96.
newsitem.headline: Texas April sales tax payments down vs April '96.

text.p: Texas State Comptroller of Public Accounts John Sharp delivered Friday a total of $142.5 million in monthly sales tax payments to 1,085 Texas cities and 117 counties, a release from his office said.

"While April sales tax rebates overall were somewhat below those for the same month last year, year-to-date rebates to Texas cities and counties are still up by 4.3 percent over the first four months of 1996, as the state economy continues a slow, steady rate of growth," Sharp said in the release.

Sales tax rebates delivered to Texas cities totaled $130 million, 2.9 percent lower than last year's April payments of $133.9 million. Likewise, rebates of $12.4 million to Texas counties were 2.9 percent below their allocations of $12.8 million in April 1996.
This month's sales tax rebates include local sales taxes collected in February and reported by businesses filing monthly tax returns in March, the release said.
Houston received a sales tax rebate of $17.5 million in April, 6.3 percent smaller than last year's $18.7 million for the month. Year-to-date payments to the city however are up 1.9 percent.
The $11.2 million local sales tax allocation Dallas received for April reflects a 7.3 percent decline from the $12.1 million in sales tax rebate for the same month last year.
Year-to-date payments to Dallas are virtually unchanged from those for the first four months of 1996.
